newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Strong earthquake rocks southern Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Strong earthquake rocks southern Philippines.

text.p: A strong earthquake rocked the main southern Philippine island of Mindanao early on Wednesday but there were no immediate reports of casualties or damage, government seismologists said.
Chief government seismologist Delfin Garcia said the tremor, measuring a magnitude of seven on the Richter scale, was centered in the sea off Surigao city.
"It came from a depth of about 100 km (60 miles) and we don't expect any major damage or calamity because it was so deep," he said.
The tremor occurred at 3:21 a.m. (1921 GMT Tuesday) and was felt in several cities and towns on Mindanao, 800 kms (500 miles) south of Manila, Garcia said.
Its epicentre was pinpointed at 32 kms (21 miles) from Surigao city.

"Aftershocks and damage are expected to be minimal due to the tremor's depth from the surface and distance from densely populated areas," said a bulletin from the Philippine Institute of Vulcanology and Seismology.
About 1,600 people died in July 1990 when an earthquake measuring 7.7 struck the main Philippine island of Luzon.
